Definition: from a shorter form of G2564; renown (as if being called):--glory.
BiblicalUsage: Kleos is renown, glory as if from being called by name. 1 Peter 2:20 asks, for what glory is it, if, when ye be buffeted for your faults, ye shall take it patiently? but if, when ye do well, and suffer for it, ye take it patiently, this is acceptable with God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Peter turns glory upside down: the renown God counts is not applause for success, but patience under a blow you did not deserve.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
